subject: Tiered credits vs fixed-fee packaging — CloudWay decision run
messages:
From: Rita Barnes <rita@cloudway.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, jordan_blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Kyle Thompson <kyle@cloudway.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Vendor comparison: pricing structure question (CloudWay RFP attached)

Hi Sean / Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the runtime performance looked solid and the team liked the cost transparency. Procurement asked me to follow up with a single ask: can Redwood match a competing vendor's blended economic that combines a fixed annual platform fee plus a usage credit bucket?

We need two concrete things to present to our CFO by Dec 3: a) a side-by-side comparison of a tiered credits model (credits used against token/embedding consumption) vs a fixed-fee + overage model, and b) an estimate of onboarding/egress risk and how Redwood would handle rollback/exit fees.

Attached is our RFP summary and the competitor's public pricing sheet. Would you be able to return a short proposal with both packaging options by Tuesday?

Appreciate it,
Rita

Attachments: CloudWay_RFP_summary.pdf

--
Rita Barnes
Director of Platform Procurement
CloudWay, Inc.

From: sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Rita Barnes <rita@cloudway.com>
Cc: jordan_blake <jordan@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Vendor comparison: pricing structure question (CloudWay RFP attached)

Hi Rita — thanks for the clear ask and the RFP. Jordan and Kim: looping you in to draft the two scenarios (tiered credits vs fixed-fee + credits) and a short note on migration/egress guardrails.

Rita — quick clarifying questions so we model apples-to-apples:
- What term length is CloudWay evaluating (12 vs 24 months)?
- Do they expect guaranteed throughput (SLA) or is this purely best-effort?
- Any mandatory security/compliance items that would change hosting costs (e.g., dedicated VPC, audit retention)?

I attached an initial spreadsheet with scenario placeholders. Jordan / Kim — primary goal: produce a one-page economics summary + recommended default packaging for an easy procurement ask. If we can show a net present value (NPV) of credits vs fixed-fee over 12/24 months that highlights a win for Redwood, that will help close.

Thanks — planning to send a draft back to Rita by EOD Tuesday.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_scenario_A.xlsx

--
Sean Gallagher
Head of Sales, West
Redwood Inference

From: jordan_blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: model write-up and key tradeoffs

Sean / Kim — internal note before we send to CloudWay. Key bullets: 
- Tiered credits (our recommended default):
  - Pros: flexible, aligns marginal cost to usage; cheaper for bursty workloads due to caching/batching; easy to apply existing telemetry for credit burn forecasts.
  - Cons: harder for finance to forecast; CPQ needs a recommended consumption cap to avoid sticker shock.
- Fixed-fee + credit bucket (competitor ask):
  - Pros: predictable invoice for CFO; simple to compare vs existing vendor.
  - Cons: requires higher upfront commitment; we should tie fixed-fee to committed throughput SLA to justify the price.

Migration/egress guardrails to propose: 
- 90-day staged data egress credits (discounted) + technical migration playbook (export scripts + KV cache persistence patterns).
- If CloudWay wants a rollback clause, offer a 30-day support credit and an optional paid professional services package for the cutover.

I'll prepare the one-pager with numbers for 12- and 24-month terms and mark a recommended default. Planning to include a 10% introductory credit for Q1 usage if they sign before Jan 15.

-Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Rita Barnes <rita@cloudway.com>
Cc: jordan_blake <jordan@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Kyle Thompson <kyle@cloudway.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2026 16:48:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: tiered credits vs fixed-fee + credit bucket (summary + next steps)

Hi Rita / Kyle — appreciate the patience while we modeled the two approaches. Attached is a concise summary (one page) and a spreadsheet with the 12/24 month NPV comparisons. High-level recommendation from our side: tiered credits priced at a slightly higher per-unit rate but with a 10% onboarding credit yields lower expected TCO for CloudWay in bursty patterns and preserves rollback flexibility. If CloudWay requires invoice predictability, the fixed-fee + credit bucket can be offered at a blended rate with a throughput SLA and an optional migration services package.

Action items / next steps:
1) Please confirm term preference (12 vs 24 months) — we will lock final numbers once confirmed.
2) If you prefer fixed-fee, we will draft a redlineable term sheet and open a DocuSign packet (link below).
3) Jordan will schedule a 30-minute finance walk-through early next week to run the NPV lines with your CFO.

DocuSign (fixed-fee starter packet): https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?env=prod&acct=12345
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/4321-CW

Attachments: redwood_final_offer_summary.pdf, redwood_pricing_scenario_A.xlsx

Looking forward — we can be flexible on packaging to match CloudWay's procurement cadence.

Best,
Sean
